searches.note: Twenty two searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, six left unspent for the run's shared allowance; one of the eight on Luís Pato, for the Portuguese wording of the Monopólio line, returned nothing. The two shared searches went to the Bairrada's demarcation (Portaria 709-A/79 of 28 December 1979, read through its summary on the Diário da República) and to the Garrafeira mention (the consolidated portaria on the Diário da República, the UK register and Portaria 1070/98). Two houses' own domains were searched by restriction (luispato.com, casadesaima.com), each read as primary through its summary, and a third own domain was found for Quinta das Bágeiras; the rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked (the house itself where the account had to be independent, Rota da Bairrada, Uncorked, Skurnik, Cave Lusa, Apewineboxes, Wine House Portugal, Spirited Wines, Hedonism, Flatiron, M Wines, Curry Wines, Decanter and Wikipedia). Writers' own sites that came up were read and never cited. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the law and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to what most needed a second source: the claims resting on one account in the author's report (the yeast at Bágeiras, Bussaco's making in its own cellar, the protest of 1999, the study of 1887), then to the houses' own pages, then to independent accounts with the author's sources blocked, and to the governing texts for the Bairrada and the Garrafeira.

Where accounts disagreed and none was primary, the figure was widened or tied to its vintage (Vinha Barrosa's oak), or hedged (by most accounts, 1917); where a fact rested on one account and the refuter found it nowhere (no added yeast at Bágeiras, the king's commission of 1887, the oldest vineyard, Vinha da Mata near the hotel), it was taken out.

tested: The vineyard, its year and its word: the house's vineyards page, searched on its own domain, gives Vinha Barrosa planted in 1900 with Baga, a century old vineyard ringed by pines and eucalyptus, and Monopólio on the label since the 2008 vintage as the search read it (the author read after); a second search for the Portuguese wording failed. Borne out, the year hedged.

The dates of the story, the author's sources blocked: the father's bottling of 1970 and the first wine of 1980, a pure Baga, on Punch, an importer's story and others; the single vineyard reds of 1995, Vinha Pan, Vinha Barrosa and the Pé Franco, on the CV Bairrada's producer page and merchants, the Pé Franco planted ungrafted on sand in 1988; the records of 1887 on one merchant, who repeats the house. Borne out, save the king's commission and the two ancestors.

The making: two weeks in temperature controlled steel and twelve months in new and used Allier casks on an importer's notes of the 2013; two years in new and used Portuguese and French oak, destemmed, for the 2021 on a merchant's sheet. The author's figure tied to its vintages.
The soil: chalky clay on one account, beside the author's two importers' lime rich clay; the reddish clay heavier than the other plots not found.

The label and the protest: the founder's interviews give the reason as the government's appointment to the head of the Bairrada's body; the early labels read Vinho Regional Beiras; recent listings give Regional Beiras or Beira Atlântico; some Pato wines are listed DOC Bairrada and two accounts give a return to the DOC in 2008.

The questions: one right answer each, distractors of one kind (four plantings, four years), the explanations teach the nearest wrong option. The house rules: the founder, his father and his daughter never named; no price or score (a Norwegian listing's score and a merchant's price met and not used), nothing volatile, no judging superlative, British, no dash.

tested: The founding and the brand, the house and its merchants blocked: 1920, three Costa brothers named José, Manuel and Albano, first trading in fine Douro wines and liqueurs; Frei João at the end of the 1950s, Porta dos Cavaleiros from the Dão shortly after; the claimed first Reserva and the cork coated paper labels, which the accounts give as the house's own. Borne out, the claims told as claims.

Quinta do Poço do Lobo: at Pocariça in the municipality of Cantanhede, bought in 1971 by one listing and 1972 by one account, replanted after purchase; its red of Baga, Moreto and Castelão on two listings. Borne out.

The Reserva's sheet: the producer's sheet as a merchant gives it, about four fifths Baga with Touriga Nacional, hand picked, full maceration in a lagar with a pneumatic treader, six months in French oak casks and eighteen months in cement vats, at least fifteen years of keeping; one shop lists Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon. The grapes borne out, the cement added.
The demarcation: Portaria 709-A/79 of 28 December 1979 recognises Bairrada as a designation of origin, after the Resolution 334/79; Decreto-Lei 70/91 approved the DOC's regulation. Borne out.

The questions and the rules: Baga as the frame of a 1985, the 1950s as the brand's decade; nobody living named (the founders' descendants and the winemaker never), no price, no score, nothing volatile.

swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. Each pick is a real house of the Bairrada with a real wine it is known by: Vinha Barrosa (the house's own old vine single vineyard), Frei João Reserva (the brand of the end of the 1950s and the old cellar releases), the Bágeiras Garrafeira (on the house's own page), Casa de Saima's Garrafeira (on the house's own page, a thin record by the region rule) and Buçaco Reservado Tinto (the hotel's red since about 1917). The author's flag on the Bussaco concession put to tender in 2024 is ruled: the wines' history stands whatever the concession becomes, and the record names no operator, so the pick stands; the integrator may look again if the cellar closes.
planNotes: luis-pato: answered. Vinha Barrosa's soils are chalky clay; the label is Vinho Regional, from the 1999 vintage as a protest, Beiras on the early labels and Beira Atlântico on some later listings, while some Pato wines are listed DOC Bairrada since. The Pé Franco and Vinha Pan are in others. The founder is never named in prose.

caves-sao-joao: answered. The brothers are not named, their dates found in no source; Frei João Reserva is taught, mostly Baga with Touriga Nacional in the vintages of the 2010s and Baga in the old releases; Porta dos Cavaleiros is now in others on two accounts.

quinta-das-bageiras: answered. The Garrafeira's label and making are on the house's own wines page and its sheet; the family is never named; the Bruto Natural is in others. The why's long lees ageing for the sparkling wines was not tested.

casa-de-saima: answered. The estate's history is given by the house only as more than half a century and three generations, and the start of its own bottling is 1992 or the late 1980s by two accounts, so founded stays empty; the Garrafeira's making is on the house's page; the living family is never named.

bussaco: answered in part. Buçaco Tinto Reservado and Vinho de Mesa are on Decanter's listing of the 2011, the category since renamed Vinho; old cellar vintages are borne out by the accounts read. The why's aged for years before release is loose: about a year in oak by the merchants read, the importer's years in bottle on one source.
